blindSummary:
This jurisdiction is where the federal "LGBT extremism" designation first produced a criminal conviction against a commercial leisure venue. A bar case (submitted to court July 2025 by the regional investigating authority) resulted in June 2026 in a seven-year sentence for the owner, prison terms for two employees, and forfeiture of over one million units of the local currency — the country's first criminal LGBT-extremism sentencing against a commercial venue (the first prison sentence under the extremism designation overall was handed down by a court in a distant region in an organising case, reported January 2025, predating this one). The precedent establishes that a bar or club can be prosecuted as an extremist organisation, which is the scenario a foreign visitor walking into a commercial venue is most likely to encounter.

This is visitor-facing enforcement: the venue context (drinking, socialising) is exactly where a visiting trans person might interact with the criminal justice system. Within the uniform federal law, this jurisdiction's finding — a seven-year sentence against a bar owner — is the strongest recorded commercial-venue precedent in the country; the capital, by contrast, concentrates raids and the first organiser prosecution.
